Description: General-purpose conversational AI for writing, research, coding, brainstorming, and analysis.
Use Cases: General Chat; Research; Coding; Documentation; Email Writing
Notes: Default general assistant for everyday work. Prefer Claude for long-document reasoning when context limits matter.
Limitations: Weaker for very long documents versus Claude. Do not paste client secrets or confidential code into unapproved chats.
When to Use: Everyday writing, brainstorming, quick coding help, and general Q&A.
Alternatives: Claude for long documents; Perplexity when citations matter; Gemini for Workspace-heavy work.
Cost Note: Freemium; Plus/Team plans if you need higher limits and better models.
Security Tip: Internal data only unless the workspace is explicitly approved. Never paste client secrets.

Description: Strong reasoning and long-context assistant for documents, analysis, coding, and careful writing.
Use Cases: General Chat; Research; Coding; Documentation; Report Writing
Notes: Preferred for long documents and careful analysis. Strong context handling versus general chat tools.
Limitations: Paid usage can add up at high volume. Prefer approved workspaces only for anything beyond Internal data.
When to Use: Long-document analysis, careful writing, complex reasoning, and coding reviews.
Alternatives: ChatGPT for everyday chat; Cursor for deep IDE work.
Cost Note: Freemium; Pro/Team recommended for heavy daily use.
Security Tip: Prefer approved Anthropic workspaces. Keep Confidential client data off personal accounts.

Description: Google multimodal assistant integrated with Workspace and search workflows for chat, docs, and media understanding.
Use Cases: General Chat; Research; Documentation; Knowledge Management
Notes: Approved for team use, especially Workspace and multimodal workflows. Not the primary default versus ChatGPT/Claude.
Limitations: Still validating as a team default. Confirm Workspace data handling before using with client material.
When to Use: Google Workspace workflows, multimodal understanding, and search-linked research.
Alternatives: ChatGPT or Claude as primary assistants until Gemini is confirmed as a default.
Cost Note: Freemium via Google accounts; Advanced tiers may be needed for higher limits.
Security Tip: Confirm Workspace/admin settings before using with client or regulated data.

Description: AI pair programmer for in-editor code completion, explanation, tests, and refactoring inside GitHub and IDEs.
Notes: Solid baseline pair programmer in GitHub/IDEs. Cursor is the Production coding tool for deeper project-aware work.
Limitations: Less project-aware than Cursor for multi-file work. Review all suggested code before merging.
When to Use: Inline completions and light pair-programming inside GitHub/IDEs.
Alternatives: Cursor for multi-file project work; Antigravity for agentic coding sessions.
Cost Note: Paid individual/business seats — confirm who is licensed.
Security Tip: Disable training on sensitive repos if policy requires. Review every suggestion.

Description: AI-native IDE for code generation, multi-file editing, and project-aware assistance across large codebases.
Notes: Core AI coding IDE for delivery. Strong team adoption and the default for multi-file, project-aware work.
Limitations: License cost and cloud features need clear policy. Keep client secrets out of unapproved model routes.
When to Use: Day-to-day software delivery, refactors, and project-aware coding.
Alternatives: GitHub Copilot for lighter completion; Antigravity for agent-first workflows; Windsurf while testing alternate AI IDEs.
Cost Note: Paid seats — treat as a core Production license cost.
Security Tip: Follow team rules for which models may see client code. No secrets in prompts.

Description: Research assistant with cited answers and fast web-grounded responses for discovery and fact checking.
Notes: Best first stop for cited web research. Prefer over plain LLM chat when sources matter.
Limitations: Citations can still be wrong—verify sources. Not a substitute for primary research on critical claims.
When to Use: Fast web research with citations and fact-finding before deeper analysis.
Alternatives: ChatGPT/Claude for synthesis; NotebookLM for your own document packs.
Cost Note: Freemium; Pro helps with higher limits and better research modes.
Security Tip: Do not paste confidential briefs into public research chats.

Description: Writing, summarization, and knowledge-base assistance inside Notion workspaces.
Use Cases: Documentation; Knowledge Management; Meeting Notes; Email Writing
Notes: Useful inside existing Notion workflows for summaries and drafting. Not a replacement for research or coding tools.
Limitations: Only useful inside Notion; quality varies. Do not treat it as a dedicated research or coding tool.
When to Use: Summaries, drafts, and light writing inside existing Notion workspaces.
Alternatives: ChatGPT/Claude for heavier writing; NotebookLM for document Q&A outside Notion.
Cost Note: Paid Notion AI add-on — confirm workspace subscription.
Security Tip: Respect Notion workspace permissions; do not move client data into personal Notion spaces.

Description: Self-hosted personal AI agent with messaging gateway, browser tools, persistent memory, and proactive automation.
Notes: Core self-hosted agent gateway across messaging channels. Keep client secrets off unapproved models.
Limitations: Self-hosted agents can touch many systems—lock down channels and keep secrets off unapproved models.
When to Use: Self-hosted personal/team agent across messaging channels and local automation.
Alternatives: Hermes Agent for similar self-hosted agent work; n8n only as archived reference.
Cost Note: Open source software; you pay for hosting and the underlying model APIs.
Security Tip: Lock down channel allowlists. Keep client secrets off unapproved models and logs.

Description: Open-source autonomous agent with persistent memory, self-improving skills, cron jobs, and multi-platform messaging gateway.
Notes: Core self-hosted agent for terminal, browser, and scheduled automations on our infrastructure.
Limitations: Requires careful hosting and access control. Misconfigured agents can run unintended automations.
When to Use: Self-hosted autonomous tasks, terminal/browser work, and scheduled agent jobs.
Alternatives: OpenClaw for messaging-gateway style agents; OpenHands for sandboxed coding agents.
Cost Note: Open source; infrastructure and model API costs apply.
Security Tip: Treat agent hosts as production systems—patch, restrict SSH, and audit tool permissions.

Description: Open-source workflow automation platform for connecting APIs, triggers, and data pipelines with a visual node editor.
Use Cases: API Integration; Web Scraping; Data Analysis
Notes: Previously used; kept for reference. Prefer newer agent-based automation where possible.
Limitations: Archived for current needs; prefer agent-based automation where possible.
Alternatives: Prefer OpenClaw/Hermes or modern agent pipelines for new work.
Cost Note: Open source; hosting costs if self-run.
Security Tip: Rotate any old credentials still stored in archived workflows.

Description: Agentic development platform designed to help developers build, automate, and manage software projects using autonomous AI agents.
Notes: Core agentic coding platform already used in delivery for vibe coding and accelerated development.
Limitations: Fast agentic coding still needs human review. Confirm what data leaves the machine under current settings.
When to Use: Agentic coding and accelerated development already used in delivery.
Alternatives: Cursor for IDE-centric work; Windsurf while testing alternate AI IDEs; OpenHands for open-source agent sandboxes.
Cost Note: Free preview tiers may change—confirm current Google licensing for the team.
Security Tip: Understand which code/context is sent to cloud models under your settings.

Description: Conversational data analyst for CSV and spreadsheet questions, charts, and ad hoc exploration in plain English.
Notes: Approved for quick analysis of sample or Internal spreadsheets. Not a replacement for Power BI on client delivery.
Limitations: Uploads leave our environment. Quality drops on messy files. Do not use client-confidential or production extracts.
When to Use: Ad hoc CSV or spreadsheet exploration when you need charts and answers without a full BI build.
Alternatives: Power BI Copilot for Fabric/Power BI delivery; ChatGPT for light table questions without file upload.
Cost Note: Freemium; paid plans for larger files and higher limits.
Security Tip: Internal or sample data only. Do not upload client Confidential files.

Description: Google document Q&A and briefing tool that grounds answers in notebooks you upload, for research packs and internal synthesis.
Notes: Approved for Q&A over internal briefing packs. Not a substitute for Perplexity on open-web research.
Limitations: Answers only from uploaded sources. Do not upload client-confidential files without approval.
When to Use: Ask questions and draft briefings grounded in your own doc packs, notes, and PDFs.
Alternatives: Perplexity for cited web research; Notion AI for writing inside Notion; ChatGPT/Claude for general synthesis.
Cost Note: Free with a Google account; Google One/AI tiers may add limits or features.
Security Tip: Internal docs only unless a lead approves the upload. No client Confidential files by default.

Description: AI presentation and one-pager builder that turns an outline into a polished first-draft deck for storytelling and updates.
Notes: Approved for fast internal and first-pass client decks. Humans still polish brand and facts before send.
Limitations: Brand match and accuracy need a review pass. Not a replacement for designed master templates.
When to Use: When you need a first-draft slide deck or one-pager from an outline, then edit before external use.
Alternatives: ChatGPT for outline-only drafts; Notion AI for written briefs without slides.
Cost Note: Freemium; paid plans for more AI generations and export options.
Security Tip: Do not paste client Confidential content into public Gamma workspaces.

Description: Web hosting, domains, and AI-assisted site building (Website Builder and Horizons) for launching and managing team and client sites.
Notes: Approved hosting and AI website-builder option for DCS sites. Keep production credentials in the DCS account, not personal logins.
Limitations: AI-generated sites still need review for accessibility, brand, and security before client go-live.
When to Use: When you need hosting, a domain, WordPress, or a first-pass AI website without standing up custom infrastructure.
Alternatives: Existing DCS cloud or Pages hosting for app deploys; v0/Lovable for UI prototypes that are not hosted sites.
Cost Note: Paid hosting plans; confirm who owns the DCS subscription and domains.
Security Tip: Use the DCS Hostinger account. Enable 2FA. Do not store client secrets in hPanel notes or AI chat.
